reviewTitle: I really loved Back Bay , but these will be my last pair
reviewDescription: For three years I had a set of Back Bay tempo 30's I wore every single day (bought them here). At work I would wear only one to answer calls, listen to podcasts , and pop both of them on lunches and breaks in to enjoy music through them or watch videos and they sounded amazing! I'd use them at home because I used to run discord on my phone. I could both talk and listen with ease. The controls were super easy. They fit in my ears perfectly. I hardly had to charge them because they kept a charge like a champ. They went everywhere with me. Toward the end of their functional life one of them fell into a sink full of water but , after drying out, that earbud continued to work like a champ. As if nothing ever happened. Finally, the day came when I had to replace them. Three years of constant use without a drop in quality is not a bad run. I'd bought my Auntie in law a set of Back bays from Amazon and she returned the favor, picking me up a set, via amazon, for Christmas. This pair absolutely sucked. Figured it was a fluke. Got another pair of shiny new Tempo 30's. They continued to suck. They wouldn't remain paired. They wouldn't charge correctly no matter how deliberately I seated them in their charging case. The mic on them would work sporadically. I'd be on a phone call and , not only would they disconnect randomly but, if they somehow remained connected, the mic would just stop working and I'd have to turn Bluetooth off to complete the call. They controls didn't work. I'd tap for Bass or Movie mode and the mode wouldn't change. So, even though they were the same exact model I'd been using for three years the features I'd become accustomed to just weren't functional. I ended up buying a pair of SkullCandy Dime Evos from the local Walmart on sale for less than what it cost me for the Back Bay Tempos and I'm sad to say they are superior in every way.
